seoTitle: How to Import Amazon Reviews into Shopify with Kudosi (2026)
metaDescription: Pull real Amazon reviews onto your Shopify product pages with the Kudosi (formerly Ali Reviews) browser extension. Amazon import needs a paid plan, not the free one; here's the exact setup and what it costs.
intro: A brand-new Shopify product page with zero reviews is a conversion killer, especially when the same product already has hundreds of reviews sitting on Amazon. A review-import app can pull those reviews straight onto your product page in a few clicks, using a browser extension that reads whatever Amazon listing you have open. The one thing worth knowing before you start: Kudosi, the app used in this walkthrough, gives its free plan unlimited AliExpress imports, but Amazon specifically sits behind its paid Basic plan. This guide covers installing the app, using its extension on an Amazon product page, importing reviews into the matching product in your store, and what it costs.
prerequisites: A Shopify store with the product already listed, matching the Amazon item you plan to pull reviews from.
Google Chrome. Kudosi's review-import extension is Chrome-only and doesn't work on other desktop browsers or on mobile.
costNote: Kudosi's free plan covers AliExpress imports only and publishes up to 10 reviews per product. Importing from Amazon (also eBay, Temu, and Etsy) needs the Basic plan, listed at $14.95 a month with a 14-day free trial, which also raises the publish limit to 150 reviews per product.

steps.heading: Install Kudosi (formerly Ali Reviews) from the Shopify App Store
steps.body: From your Shopify admin, search the App Store for Kudosi, listed there as "Ali Reviews: AI Product Review"; once installed it shows up in your admin sidebar as Kudosi (Ali Reviews). Work through its quick setup guide, then check the dashboard for review insights: reviews received, published reviews, average rating, and how many products currently have no reviews. Note the plan you're on before going further. Free is AliExpress-only, and Amazon imports need the Basic plan.

image.caption: The Kudosi (Ali Reviews) app dashboard inside Shopify admin, showing review insights and a quick setup guide at 3 of 3 steps completed.

steps.heading: Find the matching product on Amazon
steps.body: Open Amazon in a separate tab and search for the exact product you're selling. Matching brand, model, and variant matters, since importing reviews for the wrong listing misleads customers and can run into consumer-protection rules in some regions. Amazon's search results show star ratings, review counts, and how many units were bought recently, useful for judging whether a listing has enough genuine reviews worth importing.

image.caption: Searching Amazon for a matching product listing before pulling its reviews, with ratings and review counts visible right in the results.

steps.heading: Open the Kudosi extension on the product page
steps.body: With the Chrome extension installed and the Amazon product page open while you're logged into Amazon, click its icon to open the import panel. Pick your Shopify store and the target product from the dropdowns, matching them against the Amazon listing you're viewing. Two optional filters sit above the review list, Must have photo and Must have text, useful if you only want richer reviews, not bare one-line ratings.

image.caption: The Kudosi extension's panel on an Amazon product page, showing the connected Shopify store, the target product, and the reviews found on the listing.

steps.heading: Scan and select the reviews to import
steps.body: Scroll to the product's Reviews tab, where the extension adds a floating Import Reviews button alongside Amazon's own review list. Click Scan reviews. Kudosi only reads the first five pages of a listing's reviews per scan, up to 1,000 reviews with as many as five photos each, so a product with thousands of reviews still returns a capped batch, not everything Amazon has. Deselect anything that's a bare rating with no real detail; a wall of one-line five-star reviews reads as less credible than a mix that includes specifics. Click Import Reviews once you're happy with the selection.

image.caption: Amazon's Reviews tab with Kudosi's floating Import Reviews button, ready to pull selected reviews back into the connected Shopify product.

steps.heading: Check the imported reviews in Shopify
steps.body: Back in Shopify admin, open Kudosi's Manage Reviews section to confirm the imported reviews landed on the right product, with their star ratings and reviewer names intact. From here you can reorder them, hide any that don't fit your brand voice, and adjust which fields show publicly, things like reviewer photos or verified-purchase badges.

steps.heading: Publish the reviews to your storefront
steps.body: Click Publish all reviews inside Kudosi once you're satisfied with the import; reviews stay in draft otherwise and won't appear anywhere. Then check your theme editor to confirm the review widget block is placed on the product page, near the description or add-to-cart button where shoppers are most likely to see it before deciding. Test on both desktop and mobile, since review widgets are a common spot for layout issues on smaller screens.

troubleshooting.problem: The Import Reviews button doesn't do anything on Amazon
troubleshooting.cause: The store is still on Kudosi's free plan, which imports from AliExpress only; Amazon is one of the sources gated behind the paid Basic plan.
troubleshooting.fix: Start the Basic plan's 14-day trial (or subscribe) from the app's billing screen in Shopify admin, then reopen the Amazon page and refresh the extension panel.

troubleshooting.problem: Scan reviews returns far fewer reviews than the listing holds
troubleshooting.cause: The extension only reads the first five pages of an Amazon listing's reviews per scan, not the full history.
troubleshooting.fix: Re-sort Amazon's review list (Most recent, or filter by star rating) and scan again to pull a different slice of reviews.

troubleshooting.problem: Imported reviews don't show up on the storefront
troubleshooting.cause: Reviews imported into Kudosi sit as drafts until published inside the app, or the storefront theme doesn't have the review widget block added to the product template.
troubleshooting.fix: Click Publish all reviews inside Kudosi, then check the theme editor for the review widget block on the product page.

faq.question: Is it legal to import Amazon reviews onto my Shopify store?
faq.answer: It depends on the product and jurisdiction. Only import reviews for the exact product you sell, disclose that reviews are sourced externally if your review app doesn't already do so, and check local consumer-protection rules on presenting third-party reviews as your own.

faq.question: Does importing Amazon reviews with Kudosi cost anything?
faq.answer: Yes. Kudosi's free plan only imports from AliExpress. Pulling reviews from Amazon needs the Basic plan, listed at $14.95 a month with a 14-day free trial before billing starts. Free and Basic also cap how many reviews you can publish per product: 10 versus 150.

faq.question: Can I choose which Amazon reviews get imported?
faq.answer: Yes. The extension lists reviews found on the Amazon page individually, so you can select specific ones instead of importing everything on the listing at once.

faq.question: Will imported reviews show the original Amazon reviewer's name?
faq.answer: Typically yes, along with the star rating and review date. Kudosi's Manage Reviews screen lets you edit or hide individual fields after import if you'd rather not display real names.

faq.question: What happens if the Amazon listing I imported from gets removed later?
faq.answer: Nothing on your end. Once reviews are imported they live in Kudosi's own database and display independently of the original Amazon listing's status.

faq.question: What if the Amazon product has thousands of reviews?
faq.answer: Kudosi still only scans the first five pages per session. Import what that scan finds, then re-sort the Amazon review list and scan again for a different slice; one pass doesn't cover the whole listing.
